regime.paragraph: Markets moved without a single dominant theme: US Treasury yields 2Y +4bp to 4.69% and 10Y +4bp to 5.00%. The US curve saw a parallel sell-off with 2s10s unch. The dollar rose 0.2%, gold fell 1.3%, the S&P 500 fell 0.5% and Brent rose 3.1%. US high-yield spreads widened 13bp. The standout move was USD/JPY (-0.8%, 3.0x its 20-day volatility).

regions.name: United States
regions.text: Treasuries sold off, 2Y +4bp to 4.69% and 10Y +4bp to 5.00%. Fed pricing was steady at +72bp over 12 months. The dollar rose 0.2% and the S&P 500 fell 0.5%.

regions.name: United Kingdom
regions.text: Gilts rallied with the long end leading, 2Y -3bp to 4.68% and 10Y -6bp to 5.31%: a bull flattener (2s10s -2bp). Gilts outperformed Treasuries by 10bp at 10Y. BoE pricing was steady at +110bp over 12 months. Sterling fell 0.2% and the FTSE 100 fell 0.3%.

regions.name: Europe
regions.text: Bunds rallied with the front end leading, 2Y -9bp to 3.02% and 10Y -5bp to 3.39%: a bull steepener (2s10s +4bp). BTP-Bund widened 2bp to 119bp. ECB pricing was steady at +69bp over 12 months on the bill-curve proxy. The euro fell 0.3% and the Euro Stoxx 50 fell 0.3%.

regions.name: Japan
regions.text: JGB 10Y yields fell 1bp to 2.914%, with 30Y -3bp. The yen strengthened as USD/JPY moved -0.8% to 156.81. BoJ pricing was steady at +113bp over 12 months on the bill-curve proxy. The Nikkei fell 0.3%.

regions.name: China
regions.text: CGB 10Y yields rose 2bp to 1.61%. The renminbi firmed with USD/CNY +0.00% at 6.6779. The CSI 300 rose 1.7% and copper rose 1.8%.

relationships.statement: Gold fell despite lower real yields.
relationships.lesson: Gold pays no coupon, so higher real yields raise the opportunity cost of holding it. A break often reflects central-bank buying, geopolitical hedging or dollar moves.

relationships.statement: Wider Treasury–Bund spreads favoured USD over EUR.
relationships.lesson: FX tends to follow relative rates: a wider US–German yield gap raises the carry on USD versus EUR. Front-end (2Y) differentials usually matter more than 10Y.

relationships.statement: The yen strengthened despite a wider US–Japan yield gap, suggesting safe-haven demand.
relationships.lesson: USD/JPY is one of the FX pairs most tightly linked to rate differentials, because the yen is a funding currency for carry trades.
Energy feeds directly into headline inflation, so short-dated breakevens track oil closely.

relationships.statement: Copper and Chinese equities rose together, pointing to firmer China growth sentiment.
relationships.lesson: China consumes about half the world's copper, so the metal is a real-time proxy for Chinese industrial demand.

relationships.statement: Higher US yields supported the dollar.
relationships.lesson: Higher US yields raise the return on dollar assets and attract capital. When the dollar moves against yields, risk sentiment or non-US news is usually driving FX instead.

relationships.statement: Gilts underperformed Bunds, pointing to UK-specific drivers such as data, BoE pricing or fiscal supply.
relationships.lesson: Cross-market spreads strip out the global rates move, isolating what was local.

interview.question: Why did Bunds outperform Treasuries?
interview.answer: 10Y Treasuries moved +4bp versus -5bp for Bunds, so the spread moved +9bp to 161bp (95th percentile of the past year). Cross-market spreads remove the global rates move and isolate local drivers: domestic data surprises, relative central-bank repricing, and supply or fiscal news. Check whether the front end (2Y spread) moved too: if it did, it is a policy story; if only the long end moved, it is term premium.

interview.question: Why did Bunds outperform Gilts?
interview.answer: 10Y Gilts moved -6bp versus -5bp for Bunds, so the spread moved +5bp to 192bp (95th percentile of the past year). Cross-market spreads remove the global rates move and isolate local drivers: domestic data surprises, relative central-bank repricing, and supply or fiscal news. Check whether the front end (2Y spread) moved too: if it did, it is a policy story; if only the long end moved, it is term premium.

interview.question: Why did the German 2Y outperform the 10Y?
interview.answer: The German 2Y moved -9bp and the 10Y -5bp, so 2s10s moved +4bp to 37bp: a bull steepener. Front-end yields fell more than the long end: the market is pricing more or earlier rate cuts. Key framework: the 2Y is anchored by expected policy over two years; the 10Y adds term premium and long-run growth and inflation expectations.

interview.question: Why did the dollar strengthen?
interview.answer: DXY moved +0.2% alongside a +4bp move in 10Y Treasuries and +13bp in the US–Germany 2Y spread. The textbook link is relative rates: higher US yields versus the rest of the world raise the carry on USD.

interview.question: Was today's Treasury sell-off driven by real yields or inflation expectations?
interview.answer: Offsetting moves: real yields -12.0bp against breakevens +2.0bp; real yields dominated. Nominal yield = real yield + breakeven inflation. Real-yield-led moves usually reflect policy expectations or growth; breakeven-led moves reflect inflation risk, often energy prices. Brent moved +3.1%.
